title: Pressure ulcers: site, stage and healing
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's pressure ulcer, if any.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for a pressure ulcer on the right heel.

HPI
The patient is a 76-year-old male who presents today for a follow-up evaluation of a pressure ulcer located on the right heel. The patient reports that the wound has been present for several months. He notes that while he manages to keep the area clean, he has noticed significant drainage and some persistent pain during movement. He has been utilizing a pressure-relieving mattress at home and following the prescribed wound care regimen. He denies any recent fever, chills, or systemic malaise. He states that his mobility remains limited, necessitating the use of a wheelchair for most activities of daily living.

Medication List
- Lisinopril 10mg daily
- Atorvastatin 40mg daily
- Amlodipine 5mg daily
- Multivitamin daily

Vitals
BP: 138/82 mmHg
HR: 74 bpm
Temp: 98.6 F
RR: 18 breaths/min
SpO2: 96% on room air
Weight: 185 lbs

Recent Labs
HbA1c: 6.8%
eGFR: 65 mL/min/1.73m2
WBC: 8.2 x 10^9/L
Hemoglobin: 13.4 g/dL

Review of Systems
Constitutional: Denies fever or chills.
Integumentary: Positive for a chronic wound on the right heel.
Musculoskeletal: Reports chronic pain in the right lower extremity.
Neurological: Denies numbness or tingling.
All other systems reviewed and are negative.

Social History
The patient lives at home with his wife. He is retired and spends most of his time watching television and reading. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol only occasionally.

Family History
Father: Hypertension, Myocardial Infarction.
Mother: Stroke.
Siblings: One brother with hypertension.

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented x3. Physical exam reveals a large pressure ulcer on the right heel. The wound is documented as a stage 4 pressure ulcer. There is visible granulation tissue and some slough present at the base of the wound. The surrounding skin is intact but appears slightly erythematous. Capillary refill is present.

Assessment
1. Pressure ulcer of the right heel, stage 4.

Plan
1. Wound Care: Continue current dressing protocol. Debride the area of non-viable tissue as needed.
2. Pressure Management: Patient instructed to continue using the pressure-relieving mattress and to perform frequent weight shifts.
3. Follow-up: Return to the clinic in two weeks for a wound measurement and re-evaluation.

Electronically signed, L. Moreau, PA-C, 05/14/2026
explanations: Pressure ulcer of the right heel, stage 4: L89.614 (HCC 379).

distractors.why: The stage is documented: it decides the code and the HCC.
